title: The pledge under the tree
hookLine: Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged under the tree (48:18)

cards: Rewind a few days before the treaty. The Prophet ﷺ has sent 'Uthman ibn 'Affan into Mecca as his envoy, to explain that the Muslims have come only as pilgrims. 'Uthman doesn't come back. Hours pass, then days.
A rumor runs through the camp: 'Uthman has been killed. A camp of pilgrims, far from home, armed only for travel, gathered by a tree. And the Prophet asks each of them for a pledge.

teach.b: Verse eighteen of Surah Al-Fath, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance unto thee beneath the tree."
He knew what was in their hearts, the verse goes on, sent down peace of reassurance on them, and rewarded them with a near victory.
The pledge is called Bay'at ar-Ridwan, the Pledge of Good Pleasure, after the word in the verse: Allah was pleased.

teach.h: BAY'AH: A HAND IN A HAND.
teach.b: Bay'ah is a pledge sealed with the hand, from the root of buying and selling, a deal struck palm to palm. One by one they placed their hand in his. The hadith reports say they pledged to stand firm and not to flee.
Then a detail the hadith keeps. 'Uthman wasn't there to pledge.

So the Prophet held up his own right hand, said this is the hand of 'Uthman, and struck it on his left, pledging on his absent friend's behalf. 'Uthman, it turned out, was alive; he'd been held in Mecca. And the tree?
A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says that the next year, some who had been there couldn't find it again.
Later reports, outside Bukhari, say 'Umar had a tree cut down when people began to visit it to pray, so the place wouldn't become a shrine.

teach.h: THE TREE IS GONE; THE VERSE REMAINS.
teach.b: Either way, the tree is gone. What lasts is the verse, which names them as people with whom Allah was pleased, remembered as the people of the tree.
The pledge mattered not because the moment was safe, but because it wasn't.

how: Many Muslims honor the Companions who pledged at Hudaybiyyah as the people of the tree, and the bay'ah, a pledge given by hand, remains a form of commitment in many communities and Sufi orders.

games.q: your friend 'Uthman is missing in Mecca and everyone else is pledging. what does the Prophet do for him?
o: pledges on his behalf, hand on hand.
games.why: he raised his right hand, said this is the hand of 'Uthman, and struck it on his left.

practice: Rest your right hand on your left, and think of a promise you made that matters: a vow at a wedding, a promise to a child, a promise to your faith or to yourself. Picture the moment you first made it.
Then, quietly, make it again in the present tense, and if you pray, ask for help keeping it.

wordCard.voice: Bay'ah: a pledge sealed with the hand, the deal struck palm to palm beneath the tree at Hudaybiyyah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Pledge of Good Pleasure, at Hudaybiyyah.

carryVoice: Your line: pledged under the tree. The tree is gone; the promise is what's remembered. See you tomorrow.
